review_evidence: README identifies the project as Lean scripts for indexing sorries and verifying proofs; the library modules traverse Lean info trees, parse files, serialize sorry locations and replay candidate expressions in the kernel.

The only theorem declarations are four elementary arithmetic/existential statements in LeanUtilsTest/LeanFileWithSorries.lean, intentionally filled with `sorry` to exercise the extractor; TestExtractSorry.lean asserts the extractor output.
Main.lean is entirely commented out and bins/ExtractSorry.lean and bins/KernelCheck.lean are command-line checker/extraction implementations rather than a mathematical development.

source_action.content_invariant: All 10 primary Lean files were inspected by role. The only proposition-bearing declarations are four toy arithmetic/existential test theorems deliberately containing `sorry`; every other declaration supports extraction, environment reconstruction, kernel checking, logging or CLI operation. Retirement hides no independent formalization prior art.
evidence: README: Lean scripts for indexing sorries and verifying proofs.
LeanUtilsTest/LeanFileWithSorries.lean contains exactly four toy theorem fixtures with intentional `sorry`/metavariable cases for extractor testing.
ExtractSorry.lean, Utils.lean and bins/KernelCheck.lean implement Lean info-tree traversal, parsing and candidate-expression kernel replay.
source_action.rationale: LeanUtils is proof-checking/indexing infrastructure whose checked source consists of Lean metaprogramming, command-line tooling and explicit sorry-extraction fixtures rather than an independently addressable mathematical or formal-specification development.

summary: Reviewed LeanUtils and retire it as sorry-indexing/kernel-check tooling plus dedicated toy fixtures, not an independent formalization corpus.
